#4190. Treyarch Lays Off Call of Duty Zombies Mastermind Craig Houston After 20 Years

Contributor at DualShockers, former Esports Insider DACH content lead, former Escapist Magazine Germany content lead, software engineering background.

Craig Houston, the writer behind much of Call of Duty’s Zombies storyline, has been laid off by Treyarch after around 20 years at the studio.

As the development of Black Ops 7 winds down, Treyarch has indicated that they'll make big changes to Zombies in their future Call of Duty games.

He shared the news himself on Friday via X and LinkedIn, and I have to say, it’s a rather graceful message considering the circumstances. Houston said he was proud and privileged to have worked alongside so many talented people, many of whom will remain friends for life, before thanking fans for their enthusiasm, support and kind words over the years. On X, he posted it alongside a video celebrating 30 years of Treyarch, featuring footage from many of the games he worked on, which makes the whole thing feel a little more bittersweet.

He didn’t go into the reasons, but it appears to be part of the huge Xbox restructuring announced earlier this year, which is set to affect 3,200 jobs. Treyarch sits under Activision Blizzard, which in turn is owned by Xbox, so it isn’t a huge surprise that the cuts have reached the studio. Still, seeing a name like his on the list stings, especially if you’ve spent any amount of time shooting zombies with your friends at 2 in the morning.

For those who don’t know him by name, and I suspect that’s quite a few people, Houston has been at Treyarch since 2006. His first Call of Duty there was Call of Duty 3, where he worked as a video editor, which is a pretty humble start for someone who would go on to shape one of the series’ biggest modes. From World at War in 2008 onwards, he was the main writer for Zombies, whilst also writing for Treyarch’s campaigns.

He is credited as a writer and designer on Black Ops 1 through 4, and later as part of the design and creative development teams on the likes of Cold War, Black Ops 6 and Black Ops 7. Interestingly, he isn’t credited on this year’s Modern Warfare 4.

Zombies obviously wasn’t a one-man show, with Jimmy Zielinski, Jason Blundell and Kevin Drew all being a big part of how the mode evolved. Houston’s writing is what a lot of fans point to when they talk about why they fell in love with the characters, though. He also wrote the jingles for the original perks introduced in Verrückt, which is one of my favourite details in all of this. If you’ve ever caught yourself singing along to a vending machine whilst a horde closes in on you, that one’s on him.

The response since Friday has been lovely to see. Former Treyarch developer Tony Flame replied to Houston’s post calling him a legend and saying it was an honour to work with him, adding that he created a truly special experience that will live on for millions of fans. Over on Reddit, one fan described him as a great guy, noting that you can tell how much he loves the story and characters he writes simply by how excited he gets when talking about them in promo material.

Many fans argue that Houston never quite got the recognition he deserved. In the wake of this announcement, many people admitted they hadn’t really been aware of him until after Black Ops 3, despite him having been there since the very beginning, and I think that’s true for a lot of us players. We tend to know the directors and the faces from the trailers, whilst the people writing the lines we end up quoting for years stay in the background. Zombies a mode spawned out of passion, and it’s hard to see someone fundamentally involved with that leave.

Truth be told, this is the part of the Xbox restructuring that I find hardest to get my head around. Twenty years of knowing a story inside out, including every timeline, every character and every twist, isn’t something a studio can simply hire back in. Of course, I don’t know the reasoning behind this particular decision, and Houston himself hasn’t said a bad word about Treyarch. It is, however, a reminder that these layoff numbers are made up of people, some of whom have been shaping the games we love for the last two decades.

Houston hasn’t said what he plans to do next. Whatever it ends up being, I hope it involves writing, and ideally a jingle or two.

#4188. Death Stranding Isolations Animated Series Gets New Teaser Trailer

A new teaser trailer for Death Stranding Isolations, an upcoming animated series coming exclusively to Disney+ and Hulu next year, premiered during Kojima Productions’ 10th Anniversary Exhibition Beyond the Strand. The series was first announced last year.

Death Stranding Isolations tells an original story in the Death Stranding universe set immediately after the events of the first game. Isolations is created by Japanese animation studio E&H Production (Ninja Kamui, Bullet/Bullet, Magic Knight Rayerath) and directed by Takayuki Sano.  Death Stranding creator Hideo Kojima serves as executive producer.

Today’s teaser video provides the following story synopsis:

The Death Stranding—a catastrophic series of explosions caused when the dead crept into our world and collided with the living.

In the wake of this cataclysm, many were forced to live in absolute isolation—among them, a young girl. Although this lonely existence was forced upon her, she soon grows to prefer solitude, eschewing all opportunities for real human connection and allowing herself to be strung along by fate.

In Death Stranding, legendary game creator Hideo Kojima brought you a haunting vision of a shattered world. Now, that world expands into new frontiers with a brand-new animation series.

Under the guidance of director Takayuki Sano, world-class hand-drawn animations have been brought to life by renowned studio “E&H production” (NINJA KAMUI, BULLET/BULLET, the Magic Knight Rayearth television series).

The story is set in North America immediately after Sam—the protagonist of the game—reconnects the continent by means of the Chiral Network. However, as America is reborn from the ashes, the renewed connections that bind it together bring about new and unforeseen consequences.

In this tumultuous new landscape, there are some who walk a different path to the one chosen by Sam and his Bridges comrades: a wise old man who connects people through a method that defies all reckoning; a female soldier ensnared in a cycle of war and destruction; a boy who seethes with rage at the absurdity of his life...and of course, the girl who chose to sever all ties with the outside world...Fate has other plans for her, however, and chance encounters see her launched headfirst into a world she does not recognize.

Death Stranding Isolations is coming to Disney+ and Hulu in 2027. It’s one of the three planned big-screen adaptations of the series. An animated movie called Death Stranding: Mosquito (working title) is also in the works alongside a live-action Death Stranding film by A24.

For more on Death Stranding, check out our reviews for the first game and its 2025 sequel. You can also read the latest update on Kojima Productions’ upcoming stealth-espionage game, Physint.

#4187. Heartopia captures the hearts of Animal Crossing and The Sims fans to become the No.1 free download across 50 countries

Heartopia is officially the first big mobile launch of 2026, as the game grabs the attention of millions worldwide.

Heartopia, the new cosy life sim from XD Games, has officially arrived on mobile, right on schedule. If you’ve been keeping up with Heartopia news, you’re likely already aware that the game has pushed back its Steam release to an indeterminate point in 2026.

Doesn’t look like it mattered much, however, as this has already been a big launch on iOS and Android — it probably helps that PC players aren't being entirely left out of the fun, since the game is already available there via XD's own cross-device platform TapTap.

XD Games announced today that Heartopia has reached the top spot on the App Store’s downloads page for free games, and it managed to do so in more than 50 countries and regions worldwide.

The developer is celebratig by offering players a lot of free stuff. If you're feeling lucky, you’ll find new outfits and furniture in three gacha banners (Gilded Acorn Exhibitions): Polar Hymn, The Frostguard, and Coolplayism.

XD Games says you can expect regular updates to add more content, through Fashionwaves and Festivals. In fact, the first season - Winter Frost - is already penciled in for sometime in late January, and it’s going to add appropriately wintery activities like ice skating and snowman-building.

In February, a My Little Pony collaboration event will kick off, bringing new inspired outfits, and vehicles to the game.

#4185. Diablo 4's long-awaited Tower and its Leaderboards enter beta today, and there's no PTR funny business this time

Diablo 4's first big moment of 2026 is nearly upon us, and it's one feature many have been looking forward to for actual years.

Diablo 4 is about to deliver on Blizzard’s years-old promise to add a challenging, leaderboard-driven experience to the action RPG. The beta for The Tower, and its associated Leaderboards are about to kick off.

As recently revealed, the new experience launches today at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT. This is a beta version that arrives alongside update 2.5.2.

This early launch won’t offer the full experience, and it’s mainly designed to get it into the hands of players early so that Blizzard could get as much feedback as possible and incorporate it into the final version.

The beta is available to everyone, which is a nice change from the usual rigmarole players would have to go through to get the PTR build and play on a different branch. The Tower, and Leaderboards will be available only in the Seasonal Realm, however. Indeed, the plan is to build on what’s there with each future season, so it’s best to think of it as a seasonal experience.

The Tower is about as simple of an activity as you can get in an action RPG. The goal is to climb as many floors as you can as quickly as you can, all while battling increasingly difficult mobs.

You need to reach and beat the Tower’s final boss before you can call it a run. The Leaderboard will then show your time, and let you see how well you did compared to other players.

The Tower is available to anyone who completed Rank 2 of the current Season Rank. Once done, an Obelisk will appear in Cerrigar, letting you access the challenge.

The Leaderboards themselves will operate on a two-week schedule, all of which will take place during a given season. In this case, they’re going to close the day before Season of the Divine Interversion - the game’s current season - ends.

Blizzard published an updated set of patch notes that show how much has changed since The Tower, and Leaderboards first became playable in the patch 2.5.0 PTR.

Though the two new additions have been anticipated for a while, there’s not been much exciting going on in the world of Diablo 4, apart, of course, from the surprise arrival of The Paladin class, which became available in December last year to coincide with the announcement of Lord of Hatred, the game’s next expansion.

#4184. EA Reportedly Closed BioWare To Invest In Developing Star Wars Battlefront III Instead Of The Next Mass Effect

Electronic Arts shut down the legendary RPG studio BioWare last week, ending development on an untitled fifth Mass Effect game. Since then, we've seen what appears to be a leaked trailer for the game, which suggests it might have been called Mass Effect Universe, and heard a sneak peek at what Grammy-winning composer Austin Wintory was cooking up for the beloved sci-fi RPG series. Over the past week, fans across the internet have tried to piece together how a publisher could decide to shut down a studio as prolific as BioWare, but according to a new Bloomberg report, the answer is Star Wars.

More specifically, Bloomberg writes that, presented with the opportunity to develop Star Wars Battlefront III with Disney, the publisher, which went private last year after a $55 billion acquisition,  chose to invest its money into that instead of BioWare's in-development Mass Effect sequel. The publication writes that EA looked at its portfolio for the coming years and had two massive sci-fi investments it could continue: Star Wars Battlefront III or BioWare's next Mass Effect. Even though Mass Effect was well into development, and even though the Battlefront threequel hasn't even entered development, EA chose to continue with the latter. And so BioWare was shut down, and Mass Effect development ended, though Bloomberg's sources say there are other, less significant reasons the studio was shuttered, too.

Those other factors include the poor reception to 2017's Mass Effect: Andromeda, the failure of Anthem in 2019, and 2024's Dragon Age: The Veilguard, which, despite garnering positive critical reception, apparently missed EA's sales expectations by 50%.

There's also the uncomfortable reality that BioWare made progressive LGBTQIA+ positive games but was a studio within a publisher house now partially owned by the Public Investment Fund of Saudi Arabia, a government fund from a country where same-sex activity, including marriage, is criminalized, sometimes punishable by death; these harsh laws extend to other facets of the LGBTQIA+ community. Another investment partner in this acquisition of EA is Affinity Partners, a Miami-based investment firm founded and run by former White House senior advisor Jared Kushner, who is the son-in-law of President Donald Trump, a political figure who imposes laws that discriminate against the LGBTQIA+ community, especially the 1% of Americans who are transgender; Trump has also been known to mock this community in various ways. No official statements say BioWare shut down because of its progressive leanings, but one has to wonder if that was a factor, especially after reports that BioWare scrubbed diversity from demos to avoid negative feedback from EA (thanks, Kotaku).

When BioWare closed last week, only 50 employees remained, all working on the next Mass Effect, after years of layoffs at the studio.

A Mass Effect TV series is still in the works at Amazon, even though EA seems to have hung up Commander Shepard's video game suit for good.

#4183. Eternal Sword Pact tier list (November 2026) - Which class should you pick?

No matter how hard developers try, it's very difficult to balance every class. Eternal Sword Pact is no different, and our tier list will tell you which came out of the oven a little too hot.

Updated on November 15th, 2026 - Version: 6.3

Inspired by the Shan Hai Jing, a Chinese text known in English as the Classic of Mountains and Seas, Eternal Sword Pact is an MMORPG featuring massive Guild vs. Guild battles. The action takes place in a vast open world filled with characters inspired by mythology.

Players take on the role of the Demon Lord and embark on a journey across mountains and seas to unite the Demon Clan and defeat the mighty Demon God, Xie.

Eternal Sword Pact includes many classic MMO elements such as tactical combat, familiars, PvP, customisation, and a Couple System. Of course, the game also features several classes, each with various skills and abilities.

There are four available classes, and if you're not sure which one to choose, we've got you covered with our Eternal Sword Pact tier list. In this article, you'll discover the strengths and weaknesses of each class, as well as how they perform in different situations.

But before we dive in, why not check out our Eternal Sword Pact code list? These redeem codes grant useful rewards like ingots and gems, so don't miss out.

With that said, let's jump into our Eternal Sword Pact tier list.

Dragon Lancer is a powerful warrior specialised in fire-based attacks. It is both the perfect class for beginners and the top-ranked class in our Eternal Sword Pact tier list, as it deals massive damage, has strong durability, and is extremely fast. Its skills are effective for both single-target and AoE combat, allowing it to perform well in the middle of battle.

On the other hand, Dragon Lancer does have a few weaknesses. Since its element is Fire, it is vulnerable to Water and Ice, so be careful when fighting these types of enemies. Although the class is quite fast, it needs to be at close range, which can be risky and may not suit players who prefer to stay safe in the back.

Overall, Dragon Lancer truly shines in boss fights, against elite enemies, and in PvP.

Spiritfox is a graceful class that uses floral magic attacks. It uses an umbrella to fight, deals strong damage, and excels at mid-range. This mage can also transform, becoming even stronger when it is in the heart of battle. Its burst damage is excellent, allowing it to take out groups of enemies quickly.

Be careful when playing Spiritfox, though. It has relatively low health, so it's safer to stay at mid-range, especially when the mage is not transformed. Even though its skills are powerful, they can be a bit slow to cast, so this class requires some practice to master.

Once mastered, Spiritfox shines in both PvE and PvP.

Lunarborn is an archer class, so it's designed for ranged combat. Its bow deals solid damage while keeping it safe at the back, and its skills can be used for both single enemies and groups. It is a very safe and easy class to play, making it a good pick for beginners.

Of course, it has some obvious weaknesses. Lunarborn needs to stay away from the frontline due to its playstyle, so close-range combat should be avoided. It also needs some space to move properly, which can sometimes be tricky. Finally, it may take a while for him to defeat stronger enemies.

Lunarborn shines in PvE against groups of enemies, especially early in the game.

Sword Sage is a swordsman class focused on melee combat and combos. It is actually a very strong class, wielding a blade and using Frost-based skills. Its versatility allows it to be effective against both single enemies and groups, and it can summon a shield to protect itself and its allies. It is also a fast class.

So, why is it ranked so low on our Eternal Sword Pact tier list? Because this class is difficult to master.

First of all, it must stay in close range, making it more dangerous to play than mage classes. Its damage is lower than that of the Dragon Lancer, and it requires perfect timing. Once mastered, Sword Sage shines in most fights, both for dealing damage to enemies and protecting allies. And that concludes our Eternal Sword Pact tier list! All of these classes are really fun to play and powerful, so before choosing, you should consider your preferred playstyle. Don't forget that some classes are harder to master than others.

We've also got a few other lists for you to peruse, including a Legend of Elements tier list and MU: Pocket Knights tier list.

#4182. The Top 10 Best Horror Games To Play This Halloween

Humans are drawn to horror in all forms, real life and fiction. Perhaps it’s the desire to get as close to death as possible without actually dying; perhaps it’s the morality of life and knowing death comes for all of us; perhaps all our heads are just a little miswired. Whatever the reason, we flock to movies where supernatural entities and puppets on tricycles upend otherwise lovely lives, TV shows where murderous cults kill and stump local detectives, and books where the words on the page seem to follow you to bed. Games, however, go a step further, letting you enter the horror and control it (or become its victim), and you could argue that, as a result, they’re the most immersive form of fiction.

We at Game Informer love a healthy dose of horror from time to time, and we often review games like this. Some terrify us. Others… don’t. And the best ones stick with us for years and years after the credits. Below is a list of 10 of the best horror games we’ve played recently. This isn’t an all-time list, so don’t fret if your personal favorite isn’t here. Instead, this is a collection of 10 horror games ordered by release date that we think are great for spooky season and beyond. Let us know in the comments what you would add to the list!

The cozy corner of the horror genre seems to have exploded overnight, and now tons of new slice-of-life horror games are in various stages of development. That said, the team behind newcomer The Village in the Shade is no stranger to the form; they made the Yomawari series, a cute-and-terrifying collection of creepy virtual tales. The Village in the Shade takes things back to the homestead, giving you (a child who emerged from a hole in the ground and was immediately given the responsibility of running an entire farm by yourself) the freedom to plant, sow, reap, ranch, and more. Just follow the important rules: don't go out at night, don't share secrets, and don't leave the village among others. You wouldn't want to break the rules, right? You could, theoretically, go about your idyllic rural living. But as you unravel the threads of what this village is, who you are, and why you're here, it's hard not to get drawn into the strange, mysterious, delightfully disturbing truths hiding in its shadows. Just don't forget to water your turnips before you go sneaking out again.

Fans of survival horror and old-school FMV adventure games will find plenty to love (and fear) in Tenebris Somnia. When a young woman visits her ex-boyfriend’s apartment and discovers he's trapped in a hellish dream world, it kicks off a well-executed survival-horror trek of inventive puzzles and resource management to overcome dangerous monsters. High-production, live-action cutscenes help tell the story of a deteriorating relationship and the toll an indie horror film took on its creators, and they play an important role in gameplay. Tenebris Somnia may not look like much due to its classic pixelated presentation, but its scares and story captivate. – Our Review

Resident Evil Requiem is not just one of the best Resident Evil games, but it’s also one of the best horror games ever made. It features a unique dual-protagonist structure. Grace Ashcroft is timid, new to the whole “shooting zombies in the head while dealing with Umbrella viruses” thing, and is generally just trying to do her job. Leon S. Kennedy, however, is a veteran of all that and more. Requiem splits its runtime between the two characters, letting you experience both sides of Capcom’s marquee survival-horror style. Grace’s sections leave your hands clammy and your blood pressure high as you desperately try to survive. Leon’s sections leave your hands shaking with adrenaline and your blood pumping with excitement as he mows down zombies (sometimes literally, courtesy of those pesky chainsaws). The result is a Resident Evil game that blends two typical RE experiences – terrifying and tough or exhilarating over-the-top action – into one cohesive package. It’s perfect for someone who wants to feel scared and then soon after receive the catharsis of being the one in control, like being the tragic victim who dies in Act One of the horror movie and the last one standing who lives to tell the tale. – Our Review

Little Nightmares developer Tarsier Studios has a knack for delivering creepy side-scrolling adventures, but Reanimal eschews any whimsy to become its scariest game yet. While mechanically it is similar to Little Nightmares and still puts small children in unimaginable peril, Reanimal is capital-H horror thanks largely to its terrifying threats and disturbing animal-themed imagery (this probably isn’t the game for animal lovers; some messed-up stuff happens to these critters). Escaping the game’s island setting is thrilling and chilling whether you’re playing alone or with a friend in co-op. Months after release, we’re still thinking about Reanimal’s memorable final sequence, which is worth the price of admission on its own. – Our Review

2001’s Silent Hill 2 is considered one of the best horror video games of all time for good reason. At release, it was a graphical powerhouse, using the PlayStation 2's horsepower to create a setting that begged to be explored, even though every bone in your body said you shouldn’t. The remake from developer Bloober Team took on a big task in modernizing the game without losing the original’s soul, and it did a great job. Among all the recent Silent Hill releases (Silent Hill f, Silent Hill: Townfall), the remake is our favorite. The story of James Sunderland and his troubling relationship with his departed wife is complex, emotional, and – important for the purposes of this list – unsettling and scary. – Our Review

Alan Wake 2 is an excellent pick for some spooky madness, in the vein of David Lynch’s seminal Twin Peaks mystery-surrealist series. Don’t worry too much about the “2” part of the game’s title. You just need to know that the titular Alan Wake character is a not-great writer who acts like he’s really great, his wife is missing, and he got trapped in the ambiguous Dark Place. He’s only one half of the Alan Wake 2 equation, with his segments set in a dream-like version of New York City. Playing as him feels the most Twin Peaks-y. The other half is Saga, a police officer who arrives in the Pacific Northwest town of Bright Falls to investigate a murder that might be linked to a cult. You can expect more traditional survival-horror gameplay from her. But this is still a Remedy Entertainment game, and without spoiling anything, it goes places. And along the way, you can expect plenty of scares. Turn the lights down low (or off), light a candle, and sit back and enjoy one of Remedy’s best games. – Our Review

Square Enix has gone two-for-two with its Paranormasight series, an anthology of stories about the strange and occult. And while the more recent Mermaid's Curse is a brilliant tale all its own, the first entry – The Seven Mysteries of Honjo – brings significantly more scares. A group of people in the city of Honjo find themselves caught in a spectral battle royale, using powerful objects and conditions to curse one another, with the allure of a prize at the end. Its magic isn't just in the flowchart timeline, where you can hop between different perspectives and protagonists to see how events play out from every angle, but also in the gorgeous stereoscopic environments and narrative puzzles. Adventure games are a classic genre, and Paranormasight will remind you of what the genre is capable of the moment you slowly spin your camera around, your eyes peeking out from behind your fingers.

Survival horror can contain multitudes, and as the years have worn on, the genre has grown to encompass a wide range of action-combat mechanics. Signalis feels like a re-centering in that respect. It's an isometric survival-horror indie project from developer rose-engine, filled with clever puzzles, scarce resources, limited inventory slots, and looming, oppressive dread. As the Replika unit Elster, you delve deep into a remote complex filled with horrors and monsters, searching for something, or someone, waiting down below. While love for classic horror games and other hallmarks of genre fiction will certainly draw you in, the stylish presentation and devastatingly human core will keep you forging ahead to the finale. Once you've breached the surface of Signalis' retro-future super-structures, you won't be able to turn back.

In horror movies, audiences often groan at a protagonist for putting themselves in seemingly grave danger just to learn more about a cursed amulet or bloodthirsty killer. But in Immortality, you are the protagonist, and despite a lingering sense that you shouldn't be digging into the archives of these abandoned films, each eerie new scene makes you want to dive deeper. It's a game about Marisa Marcel, an actress who almost starred in three movies in the late 20th century, but has since disappeared. None of the movies were ever released due to mysterious circumstances, but you have access to the archived, unedited live-action footage, including behind-the-scenes conversations. By scrubbing through footage, you can select people or items in each scene and jump to random footage from any other movie that includes the same person or item. The approach to puzzle-solving is unique and keeps you appropriately disoriented. The mystery at the center is an unsettling treat to unravel, and scary in new and unexpected ways. Immortality is one of a kind and an easy recommendation for horror fans who want to try something a little different.

In the decade since launch, Dead by Daylight has continued to succeed, thanks to a dedicated (and newcomer-friendly) fanbase and its towering roster of original and licensed personas from across pop culture horror. The asymmetrical multiplayer title has become an anthology of horror’s biggest faces, including Freddy Krueger, Ghostface, Pyramid Head, and even the Xenomorph. Whether you play as a Survivor, trying to escape all manner of nightmare locations through stealth and cunning, or as a Killer, whose experience feels more like a hunting club, you’ll understand why Dead by Daylight has become a recurring destination for fans of the gruesome and bizarre.

Read about the making of Dead by Daylight and how it sunk its teeth into millions of players in our six-page exclusive feature in Issue 368 (p. 42), available in our magazine archive to anyone with a free Game Informer account.

#4181. The Sims developer vows "our values are unchanged," as it teases multiple projects from post-Saudi-owned EA

The team behind one of EA's most diverse franchises has issued a statement about its future under the soon-to-be Saudi-owned publisher.

In their (slightly belated) new years message to players, the developer of EA’s The Sims series of games has lightly addressed concerns about its future within the publisher in a wide-ranging letter to the community.

The letter also serves as something of a light plan for what players can expect soon, and in the future, alongside what the various teams are currently working on.

The developer starts off the yearly check-in with a statement that attempts to address concerns about the future of The Sims, historically one of EA’s most inclusive and culturally diverse franchises.

This, of course, comes in the wake of last year’s bombshell that EA is being taken private by a coalition led by Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF), alongside investment firms Silver Lake Capital and Affinity Partners. The $55 billion acquisition was approved by EA’s shareholders in December, and is set to close by the end of June.

Understandably, many raised concerns about what EA’s new ownership would mean for its people, and portfolio of games. The news is concerning for The Sims in particular, a series that’s long embraced diversity and inclusivity, and has historically been popular among women, people of colour, and members of the LGBTQ+ community.

“Our Sims team's creative control, guided by our values of inclusivity, choice, creativity, community, and play, has not changed,” the post reads, though without referring to the buyout directly at any point.

“These values inspire the decisions we make each and every day as we plan for today, tomorrow, and the future.”

As for what’s to come in 2026 and beyond, it sounds like The Sims team has multiple irons in the fire. The developer is working on “a family of new Sims experiences” that will find homes on PC, console, and mobile. Crucially, the post says that not every experience will be on every platform, in order for each to focus on delivering something different and interesting.

Future releases, of course, include new The Sims 4 content that focuses on the single-player experience. The social and more multiplayer-driven experiences, however, will instead be found in Project Rene, the mobile-first life-sim currently in development. (Despite early confidence that it was a working title for The Sims 5, it's now confirmed that Project Rene won’t, in fact, be a direct successor to The Sims 4.)

Some of these projects will see more playtesting throughout 2026, so you should probably sign up for The Sims Labs if you want to hear about when/how you can get involved.

#4178. MSI 2027 heads to Valencia as Riot reshapes Split 1 with First Stand: All In in China

Riot will take the Mid-Season Invitational to Spain in 2027, bringing a top-tier League of Legends event back to Europe for the first time since the Worlds 2024 final in London. Its one-off, expanded First Stand in China will also change Split 1 for the LEC, with the full details due in January.

Europe will host a top-tier League of Legends event again in 2027. Riot set out its international calendar on 13 November, the eve of the Worlds 2026 final. The Mid-Season Invitational goes to Valencia. London’s staging of the Worlds 2024 final was the last time the continent held an international League of Legends tournament.

For British fans, that puts a top-tier event within Europe next year. Riot has not yet given dates or ticket details for the Feria de Valencia event.

Spain’s last international League of Legends event came in 2019. That year, Madrid’s Palacio Vistalegre staged the Worlds quarter-finals and semi-finals. Valencia has never hosted one before.

China will stage First Stand: All In at the start of the 2027 season. Riot calls this single edition its largest tournament ever.

First Stand 2027 had originally been given to Southeast Asia. The bigger format took it to China instead. Southeast Asia will now host the event in 2028.

The change reaches every regional league, including the LEC. The larger event will change Split 1, just as Fnatic, G2 and the other LEC teams rebuild their rosters. In 2026, First Stand ran from 16 to 22 March, between the two regional splits. A bigger event at the start of the year leaves less certainty about how that window will look in 2027.

Riot has not yet said how many teams will take part or how they will qualify. Until then, LEC teams are building squads without knowing how many European places are on offer.

Worlds 2027 will be shared between two countries. The Swiss Stage goes to Nagoya, Japan. The quarter-finals and semi-finals move to the Suwon Convention Center in South Korea. The title decider goes to Seoul Arena, which is still under construction.

The arena was 81% built on 23 October. Work is due to finish in May 2027, with the venue opening in June 2027.

The city is backing the event with public money. Seoul has set aside 1.369 billion won (about US$1.02 million) in its proposed 2027 budget to host the Worlds final and Fan Fest, Sheep Esports reported.

Everything you need to know about LoL Esports in 2027 and beyond!

— LoL Esports (@lolesports) November 13, 2026

The 2026 calendar offers a reference point for the circuit’s rhythm. MSI ran from 28 June to 12 July, and Worlds from 15 October to 14 November. Riot has not confirmed whether the 2027 events will follow similar windows.

For LEC teams, clarity on the season opener in China is due in January.

#4177. The Video Games And More You Should Play This Weekend – October 30, 2026

Welcome to Devil's Night, the night before Halloween, where video games are best served scary. After tomorrow night – Halloween proper – no more scary video games allowed. At least not until mid-September, 2027. I'm sorry, I don't make the rules. Below you will find our weekend gaming recommendations (which is actually surprisingly light on scary games – apologies), but before that, here are some of the biggest stories of the week.

Phantom Blade Zero is one of the best action games I’ve ever played, and it’s certainly one of the most impressive to watch. Beijing-based developer S-Game uses China’s Wuxia brand of action (which was actually banned for some time during the 20th Century by the country’s government) to create a stylish, fluid, and hyper-engaging combat system. It will constantly leave you in awe that action combat can look this good. But looks aren’t everything. Fortunately, Phantom Blade Zero delivers on all fronts, with weapon mechanics so detailed that picking up a new blade can feel like unlocking a new character in a fighting game. The story won’t blow your socks off, but it’s certainly engaging and enticing enough to bring you through Phantom Blade Zero’s 40 or so hours of content. If you’re not interested in the “perfect ending,” which is the only satisfactory one in my opinion, you can complete the game in less than 30 hours. S-Game mixes high-octane combat with sprawling and rewarding exploration to create a must-play during this already busy season of games. You can read more of my thoughts in the Game Informer Phantom Blade Zero review, and if you are hopping in this weekend, be sure to check out my list of Phantom Blade Zero tips and tricks I wish I knew before starting it.

If you have any fond memories of IllFonic’s ill-fated Friday the 13th: The Game as I do, you simply must play the studio’s latest, Halloween: The Game. It is essentially Friday the 13th with Michael Myers instead of Jason, but with a decade of lessons learned from the team’s teeth carving in other horror properties and games. You’re either Michael or a citizen; the former wants to kill you and all the NPCs in various suburban maps, while the latter must rescue as many NPCs as possible while staying alive themselves. It’s that classic cat-and-mouse formula IllFonic is the master of, but with all the style, substance, and synths of John Carpenter’s Halloween masterpiece. Plus, Halloween: The Game features IllFonic’s first crack at a single-player campaign, and while it’s largely a tutorial for playing as Michael, if you’re a Halloween mega-fan like me, it’s worth checking out if only to take part in some of the film’s most iconic kills. You can read more of my thoughts in the Game Informer Halloween: The Game review here, and if you’re hopping in this weekend, there’s a new map, additional Halloween-themed cosmetics to unlock, and more waiting for you.

Overwatch is in the midst of its Halloween event, which have always historically been pretty interesting. This year it's Mystery Madness: Graveyard Games. In it, you begin by picking one of three characters in a random role. And then, as the game progresses, you choose perks that upgrade, alter, or completely change what your character can do. It can get really chaotic where by round three characters like Orisa might be three times her normal size or Torbjorn might have placed a giant turret on Mercy's making her a flying death machine. There are also Halloween skins, as well.

Tom the Postgirl is an odd little adventure that I'd recommend to fans of Untitled Goose Game. You play as Tom, a creepy girl who's tasked with delivering packages to the people of her wacky town, which is depicted with storybook-style illustrations and a color palette limited to black, white, and red. On the surface, you're delivering packages, but the game's real story is based on Tom's tendency to peep where she shouldn't, peering into townsfolks' windows to watch their odd lives. On house is full of kids who live like dogs; another has a couple with a bizarre obsession with tickling. You never know what each window might reveal, and I quickly sympathized with (and enabled) Tom's compulsion. You also have the capacity to cause quite a bit of trouble by stomping on flowers, haphazardly snipping strings and cords, or even stealing packages and using them for your own mischievous purposes. It's a pretty short experience, completable in just a few hours, making it a nice palate cleanser between the massive releases at the end of the year.

This Devolver Digital-published game has a simple but head-turning premise. You’re a profoundly angry woman who returns to her small hometown armed with nothing but a sledgehammer, which she uses to smash everything in sight. The town is also inhabited by robots possessing human consciousnesses. Swinging the hammer can either punch holes through walls or, with enough force, reduce entire buildings to rubble. But why is she doing this? Why is she so mad? A big part of Virtue and a Sledgehammer’s allure is its fascinating and well-written tale about the protagonist’s strained relationships with her sister and mother. Learning more about their lives requires you to keep smashing, but the more you learn, the more you begin to question whether smashing everything is actually a good idea.

This bizarre indie blends fun match-3 puzzle-solving with tower defense gameplay wrapped around a funny but surreal story. The match-3 gameplay involves sliding tiles to match geographic elements like castles, trees, and rivers to collect resources that feed into the tower defense portion. Depending on how the board looks when the puzzle portion ends, you send troops (sustained by the resources you collected) to attack/defend against rival castles and gather more items; board positioning determines how well this can go. The two mechanics feed into each other to create a fun loop that grows in complexity as new mechanics are introduced. Did I mention the game is also very weird? The silly tale centers on a medieval court designating you the chosen savior to rescue their lost queen (and many other tasks), and the dumb tone adds personality to a sometimes dry genre. Titanium Court charmed and impressed us when it launched on PC earlier this year, and now console and mobile players get their chance to hold court.

Sword of the Sea is a beautiful, 2025 game about surfing through the sand atop a floating sword. It recalls Journey, the emotional 2012 PlayStation game, which makes sense as it comes from the artists and developers that worked on that game, developer Giant Squid. Giant Squid also made 2016's Abzû and 2020's The Pathless. It's a talented team and Sword of the Sea maintains that reputation. And now you can play it on Switch 2. You can read my full review of the game (though this review pertains to the PlayStation 5 version) right here.

Cities: Skylines arrived on PC more than a decade ago, but is still revered as one of the greatest modern city-builders. Even now, three years after the sequel's release, Paradox continues supporting and porting the original game. A couple years after its initial release, Cities: Skylines received a strong console port, which did an admirable job of adapting the controls to gamepads, but the Switch version was always the weakest of the bunch. As of this week, Switch 2 owners can play a less compromised version, expanding the Switch's 9-tile limit to a much larger 25-tile limit, as well as better performance and textures, better control panels, and a ton of DLC and added content. And on top of that, if you own the Switch 1 version, you get a deep discount on the Switch 2 version.

While not specifically about this new Switch 2 version, you can read our original reviews of the base PC version here, and the base console version here.

Minecraft has held its dominant spot in pop culture for so long that it's easy to forget a simple fact about it: the game is awesome. This week, it's coming to Switch 2, giving potential miners another platform to explore procedurally-generated caves in. You've certainly heard of it, and you've probably played it, but I still feel it often doesn't get the flowers it deserves in high-level critical discussions about games, despite its regular cadence of major updates. The opening gameplay loop is so satisfying that for many of my peers, whether they regularly play video games or not, it's only a matter of time before they boot up a new world again. While you can never play the game for the first time again, if you haven't checked it out in a couple years, you might be surprised by the amount of new blocks, materials, and mobs they've added in recent updates. And if you've never played before, the Switch 2 launch is as good a time as any to see what all the fuss is about.

The card game incarnation of Arkham Horror remains one of the best narrative-driven and horror-themed tabletop games around, and it's an easy recommendation if you're looking for something engaging to dive into on Halloween night. Rooted in the monsters and mysteries of the Cthulhu Mythos, this living card game is built on major core sets and expansions. But unlike a TCG, each new installment has the same cards included, fueling the cooperative adventures you'll undertake together with your fellow players. Last year Arkham Horror: The Card Game did something of a soft relaunch for a chapter 2 of its narrative, and that new core set is an ideal place to jump on  play. Players each control an individual investigator as they explore arcane and weird mysteries, confront monsters, and unfold plots of cultists, ancient entities, and forbidden lore. For fans of cosmic horror storytelling, it's an easy pick.

#4176. Feed the Scorchpot serves up a dice-rolling roguelike where you cook for a dragon

Feed the Scorchpot is based on a rather simple deal - a dragon protects your island for twenty years, and in return, you cook it dinner for twenty years. The hand-drawn dice roguelike from husband-and-wife studio Moravian is out now in early access on Google Play, with an iOS version coming soon.

Each year, you roll dice to work the island, harvest ingredients, combine them into recipes and then cook them down in the Scorchpot itself. If the meal isn’t up to scratch, then it’s been made fairly clear that you end up in the pot instead.

All your strategizing happens on the island itself. You build farmsteads, shrines and harbours across a hex grid so they feed into one another, with more than 50 buildings and 80 recipes to unlock and upgrade, and the recipes boost your Flavor and Essence to multiply your Fodder score.

There are over 20 types of dice to tune your tray with as well, including odd, even and coloured dice, plus one with a six on every face. Winning in fewer seasons gets you a bigger payoff, but every extra year brings harsher odds and a hungrier dragon, which occasionally throws a tantrum and sets fire to your board.

Comparisons have been made to Balatro and Slay the Spire, which is a lot to live up to. Balatro showed there are plenty of people on phones happy to spend hours chasing silly scores, and Feed the Scorchpot is going about it sensibly by letting you start for free and unlock the rest with a single purchase.

You can grab Feed the Scorchpot in early access from Google Play now. And if you were thinking just like I am, then yes, you can pet the dragon.

Looking for something similar? Check out our list of the best roguelikes on Android.

#4175. Battlefield 6 Season 2 delayed like many of us expected, but we're getting a new update and a bonus battle pass path

Battlefield 6 has pushed back its next season by nearly a month in order to refine Season 2 content and implement more of players' feedback.

Battlefield Studios has released its first official communication in 2026. Rather than unveil the second season of Battlefield 6, however, the developer instead announced a delay. The currently ongoing Season 1 was initially meant to end on Tuesday, January 20, hence why the developer had to communicate something this week.

Season 1 will now end on Tuesday, February 17, which is also when Season 2 will kick off. Given the current sentiment around the game, this news isn’t surprising in the least.

In the blog post announcing the delay, BF Studios said that the decision to extend the current season and push back the start of the next one allows for extra time to “further polish and refine” Season 2 content.

The developer did not offer any hints about Season 2, but there’s an incredibly brief teaser trailer featuring a soldier wearing a gas mask emerging from an environment drenched in toxic gas.

Given that Battlefield 6’s battle royale mode Redsec does not utilise the popular encroaching gas mechanic (using an encroaching ring of fire instead), it’s possible that we may be looking at something new in multiplayer akin to Battlefield 1. Of course, this may just be a visual piece that doesn’t reflect the gameplay of Season 2.

Escalating the fight with new threats on the battlefield.Season 2 begins February 17. pic.twitter.com/fGMegJJuTj

What we are getting news of today, however, is the game’s next patch. This extension update is going to arrive next week, on January 20, when Season 1 was supposed to end. It’s bringing new weekly challenges to the game, but its biggest addition is yet another Bonus Path to the battle pass. You can also expect the free daily login rewards to continue, alongside other periods of double XP.

Similar to other Bonus Paths, the new Frostfire Bonus Path can be completed alongside the Season 1 battle pass. You’ll need 110 Bonus Path Points in total if you want to earn everything it has to offer, with each tier requiring 10 points. It is worth noting, however, that Frostfire Points are only earned through weekly challenges, meaning there won’t be any bonus challenges associated with it.

Frostfire includes several new customisation rewards, of course, such as a Weapon Package, soldier skin, XP boosts and the usual run of unlocks.

Though the latest blog post may be devoid of any real details on Season 2, BF Studios confirmed that Battlefield Labs will play a larger role in offering a preview of what’s to come, so it’s entirely possible that the testing initiative will soon open its doors to players with an early look at some of the maps and other content planned for Season 2.

#4174. 10 Survival Games That Don’t Make Hunger Their Whole Personality

Contributor at DualShockers, former Esports Insider DACH content lead, former Escapist Magazine Germany content lead, software engineering background.

Survival games have had a hold on me for years now. There’s truly nothing like crash-landing somewhere hostile with nothing but the clothes on your back, punching a tree, and slowly building something that resembles a home. What I could absolutely do without, though, is the little drumstick icon that starts flashing at me roughly ten minutes into every new world.

From Rain World's terrifying sights to Subnautica's oceanic survival, these are the 10 Best Open World Survival Games.

Look, I get it. Hunger is realistic, and in some games, it genuinely adds to the experience. But far too often, it feels like a chore that’s been bolted on because that’s just what survival games do, and I’m not being funny, but I didn’t plan an entire expedition just to turn around because my character fancies a snack.

Thankfully, not every developer feels the same way. Some have turned food into a reward rather than a punishment, some have made hunger completely optional, and a few have decided that your character doesn’t need to eat at all. They’re all still survival games, and some of them are pretty brutal, so let’s take a look at my favourites that found far more interesting ways to try and kill you.

Valheim is pretty much the poster child for survival games that do food differently. There’s no hunger meter, and you will never starve to death, no matter how long you go without eating. Instead, you can have up to three different foods active at once, with each of them boosting your maximum health and stamina before slowly wearing off.

Skipping a meal won’t hurt you, but it will leave you with a measly 25 health and 50 stamina, healing a single hit point every ten seconds. Considering a single troll can flatten you in a matter of seconds, that’s more than enough motivation to get cooking. Food becomes part of your preparation, just like repairing your gear before a big boss fight, rather than something you need to do just to stay alive.

Note: Iron Gate reworked the entire food system with the Hearth & Home update back in 2021, and truth be told, not everyone was thrilled about it at the time.

After more than five years in Early Access and over 17 million copies sold, Valheim finally hit 1.0 on 9 September 2026, together with the Deep North biome. Eating is still optional. Heading into the Mistlands on an empty stomach, however, is a mistake you’ll only make once.

Keen Games, the Frankfurt studio behind Portal Knights, didn’t exactly hide where its inspiration came from. Ahead of Early Access, the team said that Enshrouded would have no hunger meter, no thirst meter and no sleep meter, and that Valheim was the closest comparison for how food would work. And honestly? It shows, in the best possible way.

Food in Enshrouded is all about buffs. You get three food slots, and only one food of each type can be active at a time, which nudges you towards mixing and matching rather than just shovelling roasted meat into your mouth. Some meals boost your health, others your melee or magic damage, and it ends up feeling much more like putting together an RPG build than ticking off a survival chore.

Note: About six months into Early Access, Keen Games added an optional Survival difficulty that brings the hunger bar back. On that setting, it can actually kill you.

I think that’s the perfect compromise. If you want the classic experience, it’s there for you, but if you don’t, you’ll never have to think about it. More than five million players had already wandered into Embervale before the 1.0 release on 15 October 2026, so I’m clearly not the only one who appreciates that.

Terraria has never had a hunger meter. Sure, food exists, but it gives you the Well Fed buff, a lovely little boost to your stats rather than something standing between you and certain death. You can spend hundreds of hours digging, building and taking down bosses without ever having to think about lunch.

That changed, sort of, with the 1.4.3 update. Re-Logic teamed up with Klei Entertainment for a crossover with Don’t Starve Together, and the result was The Constant, a secret world seed that brings in hunger, Don’t Starve-style shading and darkness that actively hurts you. Hunger works in stages, and if you ignore it for long enough, you will start starving.

Note: The whole crossover started with a Reddit AMA for Terraria’s 10th anniversary, where the team said Don’t Starve Together was the franchise they’d most like to collaborate with. Klei just so happened to be reading.

I absolutely love this approach. Nobody is forced into it, but it’s there as an opt-in challenge for anyone who wants it. The fact that you need to type in a secret seed to even get hunger tells you everything you need to know about how essential it is to the Terraria experience.

Players will need to be extra careful when exploring in these open-world and survival games.

Astroneer has a pretty simple take on survival: you need oxygen, and that’s about it. Your shelter provides you with both power and oxygen, so as long as you stay within range, you’re absolutely fine. The moment you wander off, though, your meter starts to drop, which is where tethers come in to carry that oxygen with you.

What I love is how that one mechanic shapes everything else. Your tether lines double as breadcrumbs, so you always have a way back home, and the tension only really kicks in when you’re deep in a cave and very much off the grid. It’s survival with all of the tension and none of the snack breaks, and that’s exactly why I keep going back to it.

System Era Softworks released Astroneer into Early Access in December 2016, before launching the full game in February 2019. Sadly, co-founder and lead artist Paul Pepera passed away in March 2017, before the game was finished. His distinctive low-poly style still defines Astroneer to this day, and by March 2022, the game had been purchased nearly four million times.

No Man’s Sky doesn’t have a hunger meter, a thirst meter or anything that even resembles sleep. What it does have is life support and hazard protection, and both of those need topping up whilst you explore planets that are, more often than not, actively trying to kill you. Some players will argue those are just hunger and thirst with different names, and fair enough, but in practice it feels completely different.

You’re not foraging for berries. You’re mining oxygen and sodium, refining resources and keeping your exosuit running whilst dodging toxic rain or extreme temperatures. Instead of pulling you away from exploring, your survival is tied directly into it.

Food did eventually find its way into the game with a full cooking system, letting you turn ingredients into dishes that restore life support or hazard protection. There’s even a food critic, Cronus, who will rate your culinary creations and reward you with nanites. It’s completely optional, slightly absurd and exactly the kind of thing No Man’s Sky does best.

Subnautica does have hunger and thirst in its default Survival mode, so this one comes with a little asterisk. When you start a new game, though, you can pick Freedom mode instead, which is identical to Survival, just without hunger and thirst. You’ll still have to manage your oxygen, your health and your nerves, and trust me, that is more than enough.

Plenty of players recommend Freedom as the best way to experience Subnautica for the first time, and I’d have to agree. Inventory space is already tight, and every slot you don’t fill with fish is a slot you can use for resources. That way, you can fully focus on exploring the oceans of planet 4546B, which are, quite frankly, terrifying enough on their own.

Note: Freedom mode isn’t a late addition, either. It has been there almost from the start, and PC Gamer’s preview in January 2015, just weeks into Early Access, already listed it alongside Survival.

Unknown Worlds launched the full game on 23 January 2018, celebrating with a livestream from the Monterey Bay Aquarium. By then, nearly two million people already owned it. Considering what lurks in the deeper parts of Subnautica, I personally would’ve picked a slightly less fishy location.

These games are sure to keep fans of the Subnautica series entertained.

Satisfactory is a factory-building game first and a survival game a very distant second, but it still drops you onto an alien planet full of wildlife that would love nothing more than to take a bite out of you. What it doesn’t do is make you eat. Food is purely there to heal you, and the planet’s edible flora are more like a first aid kit than an actual meal.

Paleberries heal 10 HP, Beryl Nuts a little less, and the Bacon Agaric mushroom heals 20. Eventually, you can even process them into inhalers, because of course the answer to everything in Satisfactory is automation. The only real hunger in this game is your factory’s endless appetite for more power, more iron and more conveyor belts.

Note: ADA, your ever-so-helpful AI companion, refers to the Bacon Agaric as Amanita Lardum. Whether it actually tastes like bacon remains a mystery.

Coffee Stain Studios released Satisfactory 1.0 on 10 September 2024, after over five years in Early Access and 5.5 million copies sold. And the big reveal in the release date trailer? A flushable toilet. We all have our priorities.

Starbound, Chucklefish’s sci-fi sandbox, lets you decide on your relationship with food right at character creation. Casual mode removes the need to eat entirely, Survival mode adds a hunger meter, and Hardcore combines hunger with permadeath for anyone who enjoys suffering. There’s no switching later on, so you’d better know what you want before you start.

Interestingly, hunger had actually been taken out during development, and was only brought back for the 1.0 release on 22 July 2016, specifically for the Survival and Hardcore modes. In those, food rots over time, and you will starve if you ignore it. In Casual, food still heals you and grants buffs, so cooking never feels pointless.

I really appreciate a game that respects the fact that some of us just want to build a pretty space station and go planet-hopping in peace. Not every adventure needs a ration plan. Starbound can still be pretty challenging in other ways, but in Casual mode, the biggest threat on a new planet is the local wildlife, not your rumbling stomach.

There are so many great co-op games coming out today, and many allow players to just explore and relax together.

Pacific Drive is a survival game where you don’t need to eat, drink or sleep. Instead, almost all of the survival pressure lands squarely on your station wagon. You patch up panels, swap out tyres, keep the battery charged and the tank full, all whilst driving through the bizarre, anomaly-filled Olympic Exclusion Zone.

Seth Rosen, who led the game’s design, has been pretty open about the fact that a lot of his choices were aimed at smoothing out the things that bugged him about survival games. He even had pages of notes on turning radiation damage into an exposure meter, but ultimately decided against it, since you already have your hands full taking care of the car without another time pressure and distraction. As Rosen put it, the car’s health is generally a better indicator of how a run is going than your own.

Note: Creative director and CEO Cassandra Dracott’s 1989 Buick Estate was the primary reference car during early development. Her parents’ Volvo station wagon, which became the car she drove from the moment she could drive, played a part, too.

Ironwood Studios released Pacific Drive on 22 February 2024, and it sold over a million copies within a year. There’s even a television adaptation in development, and I truly have no idea how they’re planning to make a car the main character. I cannot wait to find out.

LEGO Fortnite launched on 7 December 2023 with a fairly traditional hunger system. You could already switch it off when creating a world, but for anyone who kept it on, it wasn’t exactly a great time. Within two weeks, Epic patched it to make snacks more filling, because food simply wasn’t reducing hunger by enough. In hindsight, it was the first sign that hunger and LEGO minifigures weren’t the most natural pairing.

In mid-2024, Epic added Cozy mode, which turned hunger, temperature and stamina off by default. That should’ve been the end of it, but Epic eventually went one step further and removed hunger from Odyssey altogether. Food and potions still exist and give you buffs, but there’s no meter to keep topped up anymore.

Note: Not everyone was happy about it, with some players saying the change made the game feel a little too arcade-like.

Personally, I think it was the right call for a game that lives inside Fortnite and attracts plenty of younger and newer players. Odyssey is all about building villages, exploring and fighting off the occasional Storm-Wild creature. Nobody needed to stop every few minutes to hunt down yet another LEGO berry.

These survival games are the best to come back to and explore to your heart's content solo or with friends time and time again.

Share your take with fellow players. Keep it constructive, relevant, and respectful.

#4173. Bilibili Gaming beat all four LCK teams to win Worlds 2026 and end Korean title run

Bilibili Gaming beat Gen.G in Brooklyn to win the 2026 League of Legends World Championship, the LPL's first world title since 2021. Added to their First Stand trophy, the result gives a Chinese side a double that no team had managed since 2016, just as Riot takes the 2027 season opener to China.

Bilibili Gaming are world champions. The LPL side needed four games to beat Gen.G in New York and win the club’s first Worlds title. The result ends a run of four straight LCK world titles. It also gives the LPL its first world crown since EDward Gaming won in 2021.

BLG took the hardest possible route. They knocked out all four LCK teams at the event: Hanwha Life Esports, Dplus KIA, T1 and Gen.G. Every Korean side that travelled to the tournament went home after facing them.

The final turned early. BLG levelled the series at 1-1 by winning a 53-minute second game. It was the longest game of the whole tournament. Gen.G had reached the final with two 3-0 knockout wins, over LYON on 4 November and Invictus Gaming on 7 November.

For Knight, the MVP award closes a loop. The BLG mid laner lost the 2024 final to T1. Two years later, he finished on the winning side.

The runners-up looked inward after the defeat. At Gen.G’s post-final press conference, Chovy said the team had broken its own rules. Duro, playing his first Worlds, regretted that they had dropped their drafting plan.

Gen.G still leave with US$800,000 as runners-up. Semi-finalists T1 and Invictus Gaming received US$400,000 each. Riot ran the event from 15 October to 14 November with 19 teams.

Gen.G’s admission points to the draft as a weak spot. The figures support a narrower reading too. Gen.G swept both knockout opponents before the final. Against BLG, they could not hold the lead after taking the opening game.

Worlds was BLG’s second international trophy of the year. In March they won the First Stand Tournament in São Paulo. They beat G2 Esports 3-1 in that final and collected the US$250,000 top prize.

Winning both events makes BLG the first team since SK Telecom T1 in 2016 to take more than one major international title in a year.

Our first Summoner’s Cup. It’s finally coming home.

To everyone who’s ever worn the jersey, worked behind the scenes, or cheered us on: we did it!#BLGWIN #Worlds2026 pic.twitter.com/E2TIgNfhgv

— Bilibili Gaming (@BilibiliGaming) November 15, 2026

The calendar also tilts towards China. First Stand will open the 2027 season as First Stand: All In, a one-off expanded event. Riot calls it the largest tournament it has ever produced. The event was first announced for Southeast Asia. That region will now host First Stand in 2028 instead.

The 2027 Mid-Season Invitational will be held in Valencia.

#4172. 7DS Grand Cross tier list and reroll guide [7th Anniversary]

Updated on November 15th, 2026 - Version: 2.116.0 - Added: [The Prince Master] - Highest-ranking Demon Cusack We have created a 7DS Grand Cross tier list, complete with every single character, including those who are only available for a limited time.

The Seven Deadly Sins: Grand Cross is one of the best-looking and most interesting anime games we've seen on mobile, well, ever, and as a result, it has been downloaded millions of times already.

And since we know what every dedicated gacha RPG fan wants, we aim to update this 7DS tier list regularly and keep track of every single update and adjustment that goes live on the global server. That's right - this list is dedicated to the global server, but we keep a close eye on the Asia server too, since it gives us an idea of what to expect!  How did we sort the characters on our 7DS tier list  On our 7DS tier list, we are going to include every single character, including a couple that haven't been introduced into the game yet, and rank how powerful and useful they will likely be in the future.

Of course, as usually happens with similar games, it can be tough to choose between all of the characters and build your team with so much to consider. So, to save you that headache, pick characters that are ranked high in our 7DS tier list for guaranteed success.

With all that waffle out of the way, check below for the complete list of all 7DS Grand Cross characters, their stats, where they sit on our tier list, and we've even included a reroll guide for anyone just starting out.

Before we dive right in, we need to mention that the list is sorted from SS-tier to D-tier, with SS-tier having the best heroes available and D-tier with the worst. In all honesty, you should never bother with characters that fall below B-tier. If you plan on playing the game for a long time, you're almost guaranteed to end up with some of the best characters sooner or later. Okay, let's dive in.

SS characters are the best in the game, and hence, they have a spot at the very top of our 7DS tier list. You can't really go wrong with any of them, as most don't have real weaknesses.

While the SS-tier characters are slightly better, the S-tier still boasts some of the strongest characters in Seven Deadly Sins: Grand Cross. Yes, they are by no means weak. On the contrary, they are super strong and can be used for almost all content without worry. Make sure you upgrade them the first chance you get - you won't regret it.

A-tier characters fall somewhere in the middle. They are not exactly amazing, but they aren't bad either. Most of the time, they are great for specific instances or are strong in the early game. You can invest some resources into them until you get better options, without fear that they'll become irrelevant. All in all, solid heroes with decent skills.

The characters you will find in the B tier on our 7DS tier list are in the middle of the pack. They are not exceptional. In truth, they're not even that great, but they are not bad either. You will most likely use them until you obtain better characters, when you should switch them out immediately. Some (like Ban) can be okay for specific instances or in the middle to late game, but won't really stand out. We suggest you don't invest more than you have to into upgrades for them.

Almost the worst characters in the game - the C-tier are something... special, except for all the wrong reasons. They might look good, but in reality, they aren't really all that strong. We wouldn't advise you to waste your resources on them. It's better to skip them altogether and use A or even B-tier characters instead.

Just a couple of characters meet the D-tier requirements, and they aren't pretty. Don't bother with them at all.

When it comes to rerolling characters, you want to make sure that you end up with a pretty strong lineup from the get-go. That means you need to know which characters are the best in the game, so you know when to keep pulling and when to reroll. Typically, the heroes you'll see at the top of the Seven Deadly Sins Grand Cross tier list, the SS and S tiers, are the best, and if you have the patience to reroll a lot of times, you want to aim for these.

#4168. After 15 years, The Sims' best spin-off finally gets its due follow-up in The Sims 4: Royalty & Legacy

The Sims Medieval had a short but powerful run back in 2011, and now many of its best features are finally coming to the main franchise.

The Sims 4 developers recently promised an exciting year for the game, and the franchise as a whole, and we just got an early look at one of those first events. After some light teasing, the developer unveiled Royalty & Legacy, the game’s next expansion.

Royalty & Legacy’s first trailer debuted on Thursday, revealing a February 12 release date, and showing off the expansion for the first time.

There’s a lot going on in Royalty & Legacy, which is priced $40. For one, it introduces a new world, Ondarion, which is going to be the setting for your kingdom, as you join a race for the throne. The expansion introduces Dynasty and Nobility - two new systems you can use to create your own world of royal shenanigans.

Ondarion is made up of three neighborhoods (regions). Each region has a unique theme and culture, and they’re each ruled by a Dynasty. Dambele is a place that prioritises art and community. Verdemar is a chaotic world of outlaws and nobles. Finally, Bellacorde is an extravagant region known for opulence and romance.

Speaking of building places, Royalty & Legacy also adds a new Lot type, The Backroom Lot. It serves two functions that change with the time of day. For instance, it can be a library or gym in the morning, and shift into a night club at night. Dambele has its own library-turned-rave, for instance.

At the heart of Ondarion are all the possible fantasy lives and stories you can live. The Sims calls them Powershifts, and they include some well-known Arthurian fantasies and other, more silly ones.

Swordsmanship is the new 10-level skill arriving with the expansion, which further plays into those fantasies by letting your Sims duel. There are even Swordsmanship Tournaments you can watch take place across every neighborhood in Ondarion.

Then there are Secret Passageways, which let you speed up moving across the new regions. They essentially let your Sims teleport between designated passageways, either on their own lots, or other lots in the world. Some of these are hidden for you to find, while others you can create.

In terms of new careers, there’s the Noble Career, where your Sim can rise through several Noble Rankings by doing basically what nobles had to do in the middle ages to earn favour.

The aforementioned Dynasty System is how you can join any of Ondarion’s existing families, or start your own. You actually have a lot of say in what goes on, including the usual business of appointing heirs.

Of course, no royal roleplay would be complete without scandals, which is where the Scandals System comes in. Through it, you can create stories to discredit others, or even topple an entire dynasty.

In November, you may recall The Sims 4 introducing new free items inspired by West African culture. In creating that content, EA worked with a group of Simmers who have direct ties to West African countries.

The group’s guidance was once again utilised to build the Dambele neighborhood in this expansion, and some of the lots around the world of Ondarion were even created by members of the group.

While you wait for Royalty & Legacy to actually arrive, there’s more in The Sims 4 you can jump in right now. The game recently kicked off a collaboration with fashion brand Coach that brought several free items to Create a Sim, and Build Buy. That arrived alongside a free update, which already makes for a busy start of the year for The Sims 4.
